texts: Air temperature: How warm the air is 2 metres above the ground, averaged over day and night.
how warm or cold the weather feels outdoors
Hottest temperature of the month: The highest air temperature reached during each month.
the hottest afternoons of the year
extreme heat and very hot days
Coldest temperature of the month: The lowest air temperature reached during each month.
the coldest nights and early mornings
how cold it gets at night
Surface temperature: How warm the ground or the sea surface itself is (its 'skin').
how hot the ground or the sea surface gets
the temperature of the ocean surface
Air temperature (AIRS satellite): How warm the air is just above the ground, measured from space by the AIRS instrument (average of its day and night passes).
air temperature measured by the AIRS instrument on a satellite
Land surface temperature (MODIS): How warm the land surface itself is, seen from space by MODIS (average of day and night). Land only.
how hot the land surface gets as seen by satellite
Rain and snowfall: How much rain and snow fall each day on average.
how much rain and snow falls
Evaporation from land: How much water moves from the ground and plants into the air each day. Land only.
water evaporating from soil and plants into the air
Relative humidity: How close the air is to holding all the water vapour it can (100% = saturated).
how damp or sticky the air feels
Water vapour in the air: Grams of water vapour in each kilogram of air near the ground.
how much water vapour is in the air
Water in the whole air column
Water in the whole air column: If all the water vapour above you fell as rain at once, how deep the layer would be.
the total water vapour in the atmosphere above a place
Rainfall (GPM satellites): How much rain and snow fall each day on average, measured by the GPM satellite constellation.
Evaporation (GLDAS): How much water moves from the ground and plants into the air each day, from NASA's GLDAS land model. Land only.
evaporation from the land calculated by the GLDAS land model
Runoff (GLDAS): Water that drains off the land into streams and rivers, over the surface and underground, from NASA's GLDAS land model. Land only.
water flowing off the land into streams and rivers
Surface soil wetness: How wet the top 5 cm of soil is: 0% is completely dry, 100% is fully soaked.
how wet or dry the very top of the soil is
dry dusty dirt at the surface
Root-zone soil wetness: How wet the soil is where plant roots grow (top metre): 0% dry, 100% soaked. Land only.
how much water the soil holds for plant roots and crops
Snow depth: How deep the snow lying on the ground is. Land only.
how deep the snow on the ground is
Root-zone soil moisture (GLDAS): How much water the soil holds where plant roots grow, in kilograms per square metre (= millimetres of water), from NASA's GLDAS land model. Land only.
Vegetation greenness (MODIS): How green and leafy the land looks from space (NDVI): near 0 is bare ground, above 0.6 is dense green vegetation. Land only.
how green and healthy the plants and forests look from space
lush vegetation or bare brown land
plants and forests growing back or dying off
Wind speed: How fast the air moves 10 metres above the ground.
Air pressure: The weight of the air above pressing on the surface.
the weight of the air pressing down
Ozone layer: The total amount of ozone above you, in Dobson units. Ozone high up shields life from UV light.
the ozone layer high in the sky that protects us from the sun's ultraviolet rays
Haze and dust in the air
Haze and dust in the air: How much tiny particles (dust, smoke, pollution) dim the sunlight. 0 is perfectly clear air; above 0.4 is hazy.
smoke and haze making the air murky
polluted dirty air from fires and dust storms
smoggy air that is hard to breathe
Nitrogen dioxide (OMI): How much nitrogen dioxide (NO₂, a gas mostly from traffic, power plants and fires) is in the lower air, measured from space by OMI. Higher means more polluted.
nitrogen dioxide gas from car exhaust
Sunlight reaching the ground: The energy of the sunlight that arrives at the surface each day, clouds included.
how much sunshine reaches the ground
bright sunny days or dim cloudy ones
Cloud cover: The share of the sky covered by clouds.
how much of the sky is covered by clouds
grey overcast days or clear skies
the ocean rising onto the coast
higher tides flooding beaches and coastal towns
water stored deep underground that people pump from wells
how much water flows down a river
glaciers and ice sheets melting and retreating
floating ice on the polar oceans melting
how full a lake or reservoir is
a lake shrinking or the water level dropping
how cold the wind makes it feel
the temperature of the soil underground
how much snow falls from the sky
water evaporating from the surface of a lake or reservoir
